tagline.text: Camiguin's harvest thanksgiving in Mambajao, held around the third week of October

location.label: Location
location.text: Mambajao (the provincial capital) and surroundings, Camiguin

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Around the third week of October (check the schedule each year)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱8,000~22,000 (3–4 nights, lodging, food and transport only, excluding flights and ferries)

children.text: The Lanzones Festival is Camiguin's thanksgiving for the lanzones harvest, held in the capital, Mambajao, around the third week of October each year. Expect a street dance competition, parades, an agricultural trade fair and free lanzones tasting.

The Lanzones Festival is the biggest event on Camiguin, the volcanic island off the north coast of Mindanao. Lanzones is a sweet tropical fruit whose yellow peel hides translucent, juicy flesh, and Camiguin is famous for growing it. The festival is held in Mambajao around the
third week of October
each year, and its length varies: some years it runs four days, others more than a week. In 2026 the 47th edition was reported to have a main program on
October 18–25
, preceded by pre-festival activities on
October 15–17

The festival's origin is not clear. Several sources describe it as a harvest thanksgiving that began around 1979, though the exact year differs from source to source. One guide traces its roots to old harvest rites in which people asked the nature spirits, the diwata, for a good crop. It is now a provincial event involving all five municipalities, and after being canceled in 2020 and 2021 because of COVID-19, it returned in 2022 as the 43rd edition. The 47th edition in 2026 also listed a lanzones Geographical Indication stakeholders' forum, youth street contests, an inter-agency dance contest and a Lanzones King and Queen pageant. More than 250 police officers were reportedly deployed in Mambajao and at key tourist sites.

Volcanoes are why lanzones are Camiguin's pride. The island has several volcanoes, and the trees grow mostly on high ground near them. Local agriculture officials explain that the volcanic soil makes the fruit sweet. Starting in 2018 the provincial government began marking shipping boxes with the "Camiguin Lanzones" brand, and at the time about
2,000 hectares
were reported to be planted with the fruit. Mambajao is nicknamed the "Lanzones Capital of the Philippines."

For travelers this is a festival you enjoy on the street. The parade and street dance competition can be watched free from the roadside, and there are a trade fair and free lanzones tasting as well. On the other hand, lodging and ferries fill quickly during festival week and prices rise. This page covers how to enjoy and prepare for the festival itself; for the island's hot springs, waterfalls and the island as a whole, see
Camiguin

The highlight is the street dance competition, in which teams from around the province act out harvest myths, spirits and farm work through dance. One guide says the biggest inter-agency competition takes place on the Saturday of that week. The procession moves along the circumferential road, and judging takes place in front of the grandstand at the sports complex.

blocks.title: Opening thanksgiving Mass and grand parade

children.text: On the first day of the main program, a thanksgiving Mass is held at San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish, followed by a parade of floats. This is the best moment to feel the festival's roots in gratitude for the harvest.
At the "Eat All You Can" corner, visitors can eat lanzones for free. During the season, lanzones are also easy to buy along the road and at the market.
A Lanzones King and Queen pageant and the "Mutya sa Buahanan" beauty contest are held as evening shows. Local families attend together, so it is a good chance to see the festival atmosphere up close.
At the UGMAD grounds, a trade fair gathers farm products, processed goods and tourism offerings. It is a good place to buy lanzones products and island specialties.
A children's contest, in which elementary school pupils dance in costumes made from local materials, is said to take place on the last day. Band shows and concerts follow at night.

blocks.title: Combine it with an island trip

children.text: Mambajao is the gateway to White Island, the hot springs and the waterfalls. Adding a day or two around the festival to tour the island lets you avoid the crowded times.

In 2026, the three days before the main program reportedly included government agency showcases, agricultural forums, the "Daos Ki" food bazaar and a rock band series called "Rocktober Night," while the main period had concerts every night and Camiguin's first 300-drone light show.

items.title: Festival weekend, 3 days 2 nights
items.subtitle: Arrival day, street dance day, then a loop of the island

children.text: Arrive at Camiguin Airport or Benoni Port and check in at your lodging in Mambajao. Check whether you need to pre-register with the island's QR system before arriving.
Walk around the UGMAD grounds and the town night market, enjoying band shows and street food. Try the lanzones and get a feel for the atmosphere.
Get up early and head to the street dance route. Free roadside spots fill up early.
Watch the parade and street dance competition. If you can, choose a shaded spot and bring water and a hat.
After the procession passes, have lunch at the market and rest at your lodging.
Watch a stage event or concert at the grandstand, or see the sunset from a beachfront lodging.
Take the first boat to White Island or visit the hot springs and waterfalls, then head back in the afternoon.
The festival schedule changes every year. The official program usually comes out two to four weeks before the event.
There is reportedly no direct flight from Manila to Camiguin Airport (CGM), so many travelers connect through Cebu. Cebu to Camiguin takes about
50 minutes
on a direct Cebgo flight.
Another way is to fly from Manila to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) in Cagayan de Oro and continue by bus and ferry.
Camiguin flights have few seats and their frequency changes, so book tickets early for the festival period.

items.title: By bus and ferry from Cagayan de Oro

children.text: Take a bus from the Agora terminal in Cagayan de Oro to Balingoan. It takes about
2–2 hours 30 minutes
and costs about
From Balingoan port, the ferry to Benoni port on Camiguin takes about
1 hour
and costs about
one way. In the days before the festival, queues at Balingoan can be long.
From Benoni, continue to Mambajao by jeepney or habal-habal (motorcycle taxi).
Camiguin is reported to operate a QR pre-registration system for arrivals (CleanCamiguinQR). Check the official notice before you leave to see whether it is in force and what the conditions are.
Tricycles and multicabs run in Mambajao town. From a lodging on Agoho Beach to the festival grounds it is about
10 minutes
by multicab.
Motorbike rental is reported to run about
per day. Roads are closed on parade day, so be ready to walk.
The festival is held around the
third week of October
. The lanzones season generally runs
August–December
, and one account says October is the peak, so the fruit is said to taste best during the festival. The exact schedule changes every year, so check the official program.

October is near the end of the rainy season, so showers can be frequent. Bring a raincoat and a waterproof bag. In the days just after the festival, the fair and the island are much quieter and easier to enjoy.

items.label: Lodging (regular rates)
items.note: Guesthouses to beach resorts, reportedly two to three times higher in festival week

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

During festival week, lodging in Mambajao town and on Agoho Beach fills first. One guide advises booking three to six months ahead and says some places charge two to three times their usual rates. Your lodging may need to be on the accredited list of the island's QR registration system for registration to work, so check before booking. Agoho Beach is about
10 minutes
from town by multicab and suits travelers who want a quieter place by the sea.

The center of the food scene is, of course, lanzones. Eating the fresh fruit is best; it is sold by the bag along the road and at the market, and there are also sugar-preserved products. Common meals are grilled fish, kilawin (fish cured in vinegar) and squid dishes, at about
per meal. Camiguin pastel, a bread filled with custard or ube cream, is the island's snack and a good thing to buy at the market.
On the street dance day, it is best to claim a spot between 5:30 and 6:00 am. One guide recommended this time.
The grandstand sits in front of the judges, so you see the whole choreography, but it may be ticketed. You can watch from the roadside first and decide later.
Bring water, a hat, sunscreen, rain gear, a power bank and ID. Leave your belongings at the lodging and carry only a little cash.
Roads are blocked on parade day, so finish any motorbike or vehicle trips early.
A QR pre-registration system for arrivals (CleanCamiguinQR) is reported to exist, so check it about 48 to 72 hours before departure and save the QR image offline.
Dress modestly at the church Mass and do not walk through performing teams.
The provincial government stresses a CLAYGO (Clean As You Go) policy. Put your trash in the designated places.
If you stay one extra day after the festival ends, you can enjoy sightseeing on the island at a relaxed pace.

For photos, the stretch where the street dance procession starts at the plaza is relatively roomy, and the area in front of the grandstand is said to be good for seeing the whole choreography. Splitting the two between morning and midday works well.
Lodging, ferries and flights are all crowded in festival week. Queues at Balingoan can grow long, so take an early boat and plan the itinerary after checking the flight schedule.
The schedule and program change every year. Confirm dates and venues with the latest notice from the Camiguin provincial tourism office.
October can bring typhoons and showers. Check the forecast and leave one spare day in case boats stop running.
Watch out for pickpockets and lost phones on crowded roadsides.
Prices change every year. For lodging and motorbike rental, confirm the price and deposit conditions in advance.
Hibok-Hibok is an active volcano. Check the notices of the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS).
Eat and drink only at places with reliable hygiene. Be careful with iced drinks sold on the street.
The whole island, including the hot springs, waterfalls and Mantigue Island, is covered under
Camiguin
. Mambajao is the center of the island's north.
An uninhabited sandbar off Mambajao, about
10 minutes
by bangka from the Yumbing pier. It makes a good morning trip the day after the festival.

blocks.title: Sunken Cemetery & Guiob Church Ruins, Camiguin

children.text: A cross stands in the sea off the western side of the island. Visit in the afternoon or at sunset between festival events.
